Manifest verdict NEEDS_REVISION — blocker: "missing shard result for shard-01" (all 16 files unreviewed by the shard pass)
Runtime not assessed — static-only review; no build/test/typecheck evidence

packages/trpc/.../addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (not just organizer/team admin) can add arbitrary guests, forwarding booking description, location, attendee roster, video meeting URL and meetingPassword to any address, with no organizer approval. Strictly wider capability than sibling mutations (editLocation, confirm).

addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array has no .min(1)/.max(N)/dedupe/trim/lowercase, and _router.tsx:79 adds no checkRateLimitAndThrowError. One authed request → unbounded createMany + one email per address: mass-mail amplification / spam relay on Cal.com SMTP reputation.

addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Duplicates *within* the input array are never filtered server-side (only against existing attendees). ["x@y.com" ×500] creates 500 attendee rows and 500 emails; the uniqueness check exists only client-side (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26) and is bypassed by calling the mutation directly.
addGuests.handler.ts:70-77 — Blacklist bypass: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased but `guest` is compared raw and untrimmed, so "Blocked@Example.com" defeats the operator's block list entirely.

addGuests.handler.ts:26 — No status filter in the Prisma where clause and no status check: guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED/PENDING/past bookings, each shipping an ICS with status "CONFIRMED" plus videoCallData (url + meetingPassword).

addGuests.handler.ts:44 vs :55 — Enumeration oracle: NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN distinguishes existing from nonexistent sequential integer bookingIds, and AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 surfaces the raw code+message.

addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — catch swallows err with a bare console.log string: no actor, bookingId, or outcome. No audit trail for who added which guests, making the above paths undetectable after the fact.
Correctness bugs**

[lens/completeness][lens/intent] addGuests.handler.ts:46 — `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` is AND where the variable name and intent say OR; collapses to "is owner", so team admins who aren't owners are denied. Fails closed, but the admin branch is dead.

[lens/completeness][lens/intent] addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Passes raw `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`. An address filtered out as already-attending is classified "new" at email-manager.ts:541 and re-sent a full AttendeeScheduledEmail invite though nothing changed for them.

[lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Attendee dedupe (`guest === attendee.email`) and email-manager.ts:541 (`newGuests.includes`) are case-sensitive, so Foo@Bar.com is inserted alongside an existing foo@bar.com and picks the wrong email template.
addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Attendee authorization compares emails case-sensitively; a legitimate attendee whose stored email differs in case is denied.

[lens/scope][lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:55 — TRPCError message "you_do_not_have_permission" is not a key in en/common.json (existing key is `dont_have_permission`:1628). Dialog renders t(err.message) → user sees literal "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission".

email-manager.ts:524-547 — sendAddGuestsEmails is the only sender in the file ignoring eventTypeDisableHostEmail / eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail; sendLocationChangeEmails directly above gates on both. Email-suppression settings are bypassed.

[lens/completeness][lens/intent] packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:26 — Unguarded `calEvent.attendees[0].name`; new guests are stored with name:"" (handler:85), so the subject renders "Guests Added: <type> with  at <date>".
packages/emails/email-manager.ts:531-537 — Team-member branch is dead code for the only caller: addGuests.handler.ts never sets evt.team, so team hosts are never notified for team bookings.
packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:22,44 — List is keyed by array index while removal splices; deleting a row shifts every subsequent input's identity and React reuses the wrong DOM/input state.
[lens/architecture] AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33 — isInvalidEmail is never cleared on edit or on subsequent successful parse (only on Cancel), leaving a stale "Emails must be unique and valid" error.

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49 — Dead guard: multiEmailValue.length === 0 is unreachable (state initializes to [""]); the empty string instead fails email validation, so an untouched dialog shows the invalid-email error.

[lens/intent] AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always truthy, so the t("unable_to_add_guests") fallback (and its new i18n key) is dead code and users see raw error codes.

[lens/security] addGuests.handler.ts:74-106 — Check-then-insert TOCTOU: existence checked in app memory, then createMany runs with no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and no migration in this diff. Concurrent calls both pass and both insert.

addGuests.handler.ts:92-171 — Non-transactional, non-idempotent multi-system write with no idempotency key: DB commit → external calendar mutation → emails. A throw from updateCalendarAttendees leaves attendees persisted with the remote calendar un-updated, no rollback, and a client retry double-inserts.
addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 — Nested linear scan (guests.filter × attendees.some) where a Set of normalized emails is O(1); same pattern in email-manager.ts:541 per attendee.

addGuests.handler.ts:47,60 — Magic sentinel `0` for "no team"/"no user" (teamId ?? 0, userId || 0) fires real DB lookups against id 0; a booking with null userId surfaces a raw Prisma error from findFirstOrThrow rather than a typed TRPCError.

addGuests.handler.ts:35-40,58-68 — booking.user is fetched with destinationCalendar and credentials (encrypted key blobs) and never read, then a second findFirstOrThrow re-fetches the same organizer. Redundant round-trip plus over-fetch of secrets.

[lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:83-106,145 — Seated events: bare Attendee rows created with no BookingSeat rows and no seatsPerTimeSlot check, though the handler reads the seats fields to decorate the email. Capacity can be exceeded; seat-linked flows see orphan attendees.

[lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:92-106 — booking.responses (which carries the guest list as typed data inside JSON) is not updated, so the two representations diverge; flows that rebuild attendees from responses drop the added guests.

addGuests.handler.ts:124-147 — CalendarEvent is hand-assembled instead of using the shared builder used by handleNewBooking/editLocation; result lacks team, eventTypeId, iCalUID/iCalSequence, bookingFields/responses.

[lens/architecture][lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 — EventManager is built from the acting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)), not the organizer's, though the organizer's credentials are already fetched at :36 and discarded. On exactly the attendee and team-admin paths the handler authorizes, no credential matches booking.references, so the calendar/video update silently no-ops and new guests never get a real calendar invite.

[lens/intent] addGuests.handler.ts:138 — Recurring bookings: evt.recurringEvent is populated from the event type so emails/ICS describe a series, but only the single bookingId row is updated; no recurringEventId handling.
addGuests.handler.ts:165 — No webhook or workflow trigger fired for the booking change, so integrations and workflows never learn about added guests.
addGuests.handler.ts:96 — No bookingReference/metadata update for video providers; Zoom/Meet participant lists are not updated.

addGuests.handler.ts:165 — updateCalendarAttendees is outside any try/catch and runs after the DB commit; a provider failure surfaces as a mutation error even though guests were persisted, with no partial-success feedback.
addGuests.handler.ts:85 — New guests inherit organizer.locale, so guest-facing emails are localized to the organizer's language rather than defaulting to en.

(repo-wide) — Zero tests: no unit tests for addGuestsHandler (permissions, dedupe, blacklist, empty-result 400) and no e2e coverage, despite new data-testid attributes (add_members, add-emails, add-another-email) apparently added for them.
docs/tasks/task-001.md:1 — Intent is "guest management" (add/list/remove) but the change is add-only: no remove or list path in handler, router, or UI.

[lens/completeness] BookingListItem.tsx:193 — The action is appended to editBookingActions unconditionally, which is rendered for past bookings (lines 553-554) and unconfirmed ones, so "Add guests" is offered on past/unconfirmed bookings and fires CONFIRMED invites for events that already happened.

[lens/intent][lens/completeness] BookingListItem.tsx:194 / AddGuestsDialog.tsx:98 — Action id and data-testid are `add_members`, naming team members rather than guests; every sibling id in editBookingActions matches its behavior (change_location, reschedule_request), and a real members/reassign action already exists in the same menu.

[lens/scope][lens/architecture][lens/intent] packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 — Component inside packages/ui imports its own barrel (@calcom/ui) while index.tsx:153 re-exports it: a module cycle that survives only because MultiEmailLazy defers via next/dynamic, and which pulls the whole UI barrel into the lazy chunk. Sibling form components import relatively.

packages/ui/form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx:3 — Copy-pasted comment "These are like 40kb that not every user needs" from PhoneInputLazy/AddressInputLazy, which wrap heavy third-party libs; MultiEmail is ~90 lines with no third-party dependency, so both the claim and the extra dynamic-import wrapper are unjustified.

[lens/architecture] AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — A second, differently-shaped schema is declared in the component body under the same name as the server schema (ZAddGuestsInputSchema), recreated every render, splitting validation ownership — and the client-only copy is the one carrying the uniqueness refine.
docs/tasks/task-001.md:1 — The harness task prompt file is committed as repo documentation; it is not part of the feature and should not land.

[lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:170 — console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") discards err and uses console.log rather than the project logger; the handler still returns success, so total email failure is invisible to users and operators.

The most serious items are the security cluster: any attendee can push booking details plus the video URL and meeting password to arbitrary addresses, the unbounded/undeduped guest array with no rate limit turns the endpoint into a mail amplifier, and the missing booking-status guard lets that happen on cancelled bookings. The deterministic gate returned PASS_ADVISORY and found none of these — its own manifest flags shard-01 as unreviewed, so that PASS carries no signal here.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/.../addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (not just organizer/team admin) can add arbitrary guests, forwarding booking description, location, attendee roster, video meeting URL and meetingPassword to any address, with no organizer approval. Strictly wider capability than sibling mutations (editLocation, confirm).

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly authorizes the caller if they are an attendee of the booking: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then allows the operation unless `(!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`. That means any existing attendee can add arbitrary email addresses (subject only to not already being an attendee and not being in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`). The handler then constructs a full `CalendarEvent` including `description`, `location`, full `attendees` list, and `videoCallData` (including `meetingPassword` when present) and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which will send emails/invites to attendees/new guests. There is no organizer-approval step or restriction limiting this to organizer/admin roles, so the finding describes a real capability expansion introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:5 — guests array has no .min(1)/.max(N)/dedupe/trim/lowercase, and _router.tsx:79 adds no checkRateLimitAndThrowError. One authed request → unbounded createMany + one email per address: mass-mail amplification / spam relay on Cal.com SMTP reputation.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.schema.ts` the input is `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.min(1)`, no upper bound, and no server-side dedupe/normalization. In `addGuests.handler.ts` the mutation directly uses `createMany` with `uniqueGuests` derived from the raw array but only filtered against existing attendees/blacklist (it does not dedupe within the request), so a single request can insert an arbitrarily large number of attendee rows and also trigger `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which sends emails to organizer/team members and iterates attendees to send attendee emails. In `_router.tsx` the new `addGuests` authed mutation adds no explicit rate limiting/abuse protection. This combination is a concrete mass-mail/DoS amplification risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:26 — No status filter in the Prisma where clause and no status check: guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED/PENDING/past bookings, each shipping an ICS with status "CONFIRMED" plus videoCallData (url + meetingPassword).

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and performs no subsequent check on any booking lifecycle field (e.g., cancelled/rejected/pending) or time-based check (e.g., `startTime` already in the past) before (1) adding attendees in DB, (2) calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and (3) sending emails. The newly added email templates always generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (see `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) and the handler includes `evt.videoCallData` (including `meetingPassword`) whenever a video reference exists. So the diff verifiably allows adding guests and sending “CONFIRMED” ICS + video details without any status/time gating.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:44 vs :55 — Enumeration oracle: NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN distinguishes existing from nonexistent sequential integer bookingIds, and AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 surfaces the raw code+message.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the handler first looks up the booking by id and throws `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: "booking_not_found" })` when missing, but for an existing booking where the caller lacks access it throws `TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" })`. This difference allows an authenticated caller to distinguish “booking exists” vs “doesn’t exist” for arbitrary numeric `bookingId` values (an enumeration oracle). In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, the client explicitly surfaces the raw `err.data?.code` along with `t(err.message)` in the toast (`const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`), making the oracle visible to the user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — catch swallows err with a bare console.log string: no actor, bookingId, or outcome. No audit trail for who added which guests, making the above paths undetectable after the fact.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the call to sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is wrapped in a try/catch that catches all errors and only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err` or any context (e.g., bookingId, user/actor, guests). This both swallows the exception (no rethrow/return error) and discards diagnostic/audit-relevant information, making email-send failures hard to investigate from logs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/completeness][lens/intent] addGuests.handler.ts:46 — `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` is AND where the variable name and intent say OR; collapses to "is owner", so team admins who aren't owners are denied. Fails closed, but the admin branch is dead.
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission-check bug: using `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` incorrectly requires both roles, effectively denying admins who aren’t owners. This matches the golden comment’s point that it should be OR (||).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/completeness][lens/intent] addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Passes raw `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`. An address filtered out as already-attending is classified "new" at email-manager.ts:541 and re-sent a full AttendeeScheduledEmail invite though nothing changed for them.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, guests are filtered into uniqueGuests before updating the booking attendees (only uniqueGuests are created). However, the handler calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the raw, unfiltered input. In email-manager.ts sendAddGuestsEmails uses the passed list (newGuests) to decide per attendee whether to send AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. If the user submitted an email that was already an attendee, that attendee will still be in `calendarEvent.attendees` and will match the raw `guests` list, causing them to be treated as “new” and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail again despite not being newly added. Passing uniqueGuests would avoid this misclassification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Attendee dedupe (`guest === attendee.email`) and email-manager.ts:541 (`newGuests.includes`) are case-sensitive, so Foo@Bar.com is inserted alongside an existing foo@bar.com and picks the wrong email template.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts, the dedupe check `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive and no normalization is applied, so an existing attendee `foo@bar.com` will not block adding `Foo@Bar.com`, leading to duplicate attendee rows differing only by case. Likewise, in email-manager.ts `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is also case-sensitive; if the stored attendee email casing differs from the casing in `newGuests` (the input list passed to sendAddGuestsEmails), the code can misclassify an attendee as “new” vs “existing” and send the wrong template. Both behaviors are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Attendee authorization compares emails case-sensitively; a legitimate attendee whose stored email differs in case is denied.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the attendee authorization check is `booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)`, which is a case-sensitive string comparison. If the stored attendee email and the authenticated user email differ only by letter case (common with emails), `isAttendee` becomes false and the user can be incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN. The diff shows no normalization (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`) on either side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/scope][lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:55 — TRPCError message "you_do_not_have_permission" is not a key in en/common.json (existing key is `dont_have_permission`:1628). Dialog renders t(err.message) → user sees literal "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission".

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new TRPCError message string `you_do_not_have_permission` (addGuests.handler.ts) and the UI toasts `t(err.message)` (AddGuestsDialog), so a missing i18n key would surface as a literal string. However, from the provided diff alone we cannot verify that `you_do_not_have_permission` is actually absent from `en/common.json` (only a small portion of that JSON file is shown, and the key could already exist elsewhere). Therefore the finding relies on repository context not proven by the diff.

matched_golden_ids: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue states that `sendAddGuestsEmails` bypasses the event type email-suppression flags (`eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`), matching the golden concern that it does not respect `disableStandardEmails` metadata and may send emails when standard emails are disabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/completeness][lens/intent] packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:26 — Unguarded `calEvent.attendees[0].name`; new guests are stored with name:"" (handler:85), so the subject renders "Guests Added: <type> with  at <date>".

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts` the subject line interpolates `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without any fallback/guard. In the new `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly added guests are persisted with `name: ""` (see `guestsFullDetails`), and `evt.attendees` is built directly from the booking attendees records. If the first attendee in `calEvent.attendees` is a newly added guest (or any attendee with an empty name), the subject will render with a blank “with  at …”. This is a verifiable correctness defect introduced by the diff (and also risks a runtime error if `attendees[0]` is ever undefined).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:531-537 — Team-member branch is dead code for the only caller: addGuests.handler.ts never sets evt.team, so team hosts are never notified for team bookings.

adjudication.rationale: The new `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` logic in `packages/emails/email-manager.ts` only notifies additional team members inside `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }`. The only added caller in this diff (`addGuests.handler.ts`) constructs `evt: CalendarEvent` without any `team` field (it sets `organizer`, `attendees`, `destinationCalendar`, etc., but never `evt.team`). Therefore `formatCalEvent(calEvent)` cannot have `team.members` (based on the passed object), so the team-member notification loop will never execute for this mutation, meaning team hosts/members won’t be emailed even for team bookings (despite the code clearly intending to do so).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:22,44 — List is keyed by array index while removal splices; deleting a row shifts every subsequent input's identity and React reuses the wrong DOM/input state.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx the list renders `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}> ...)` and removal does `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. When an item is removed, all subsequent items shift indices, so their React keys change and React will reuse/move the underlying component/DOM nodes for the next items. This can cause the “wrong” input instance/state (focus/cursor position, any internal EmailField state, validation UI, etc.) to appear to jump to a different email row after deletions. The problem is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/architecture] AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33 — isInvalidEmail is never cleared on edit or on subsequent successful parse (only on Cancel), leaving a stale "Emails must be unique and valid" error.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler. It is not cleared when the user edits the emails (no `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` in `MultiEmail`/`setMultiEmailValue` updates), nor when validation later succeeds, nor on successful mutation (`onSuccess` closes dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`). Because the dialog component stays mounted and `onOpenChange` can close/reopen it without resetting this flag, the "Emails must be unique and valid" error can remain visible/stale across edits or future openings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49 — Dead guard: multiEmailValue.length === 0 is unreachable (state initializes to [""]); the empty string instead fails email validation, so an untouched dialog shows the invalid-email error.
matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same root problem: the state is initialized as [""] instead of an empty array, making empty-state logic (length===0) ineffective and causing validation/invalid-email behavior from the empty string. The golden suggests starting with [] and handling empty state in the component, which aligns with the candidate’s diagnosis.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/intent] AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always truthy, so the t("unable_to_add_guests") fallback (and its new i18n key) is dead code and users see raw error codes.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, `message` is built with a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. Template literals always produce a string (e.g., `"undefined: something"`), which is truthy even when `err.data?.code` is undefined. Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback, making that fallback (and effectively the new i18n key for it in this context) dead code. The toast will also include the raw error code (or `undefined`) prefix.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/security] addGuests.handler.ts:74-106 — Check-then-insert TOCTOU: existence checked in app memory, then createMany runs with no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and no migration in this diff. Concurrent calls both pass and both insert.

adjudication.rationale: The handler does perform a read (`findFirst` incl. attendees) and later a write (`booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`) based on that earlier snapshot, so a race *could* exist in theory. However, the proposed finding asserts there is “no unique constraint on (bookingId, email)” and that duplicates can be inserted. The diff does not show the Prisma schema/migrations for the attendees table, so we cannot verify whether such a unique constraint already exists (in which case concurrent inserts would fail rather than duplicate). Because the key premise (no DB constraint) is not verifiable from this diff, the finding overstates what can be concluded from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:92-171 — Non-transactional, non-idempotent multi-system write with no idempotency key: DB commit → external calendar mutation → emails. A throw from updateCalendarAttendees leaves attendees persisted with the remote calendar un-updated, no rollback, and a client retry double-inserts.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler performs a DB write (prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany) and only afterwards calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) (an external side effect). That call is not wrapped in try/catch and there is no transaction/rollback mechanism spanning the DB + external calendar + email send. So if updateCalendarAttendees throws, the request fails after persisting new attendees, leaving the remote calendar un-updated (inconsistent state). The finding’s “client retry double-inserts” part is less clearly true because a subsequent retry re-fetches booking.attendees and filters existing emails out, likely resulting in uniqueGuests=[] and a BAD_REQUEST rather than duplicate inserts, but the partial multi-system write risk is real and directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 — Nested linear scan (guests.filter × attendees.some) where a Set of normalized emails is O(1); same pattern in email-manager.ts:541 per attendee.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain the described nested linear scans: in addGuests.handler.ts `guests.filter(... booking.attendees.some(...))` is O(guests × attendees), and in email-manager.ts `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` inside `attendees.map(...)` is O(attendees × newGuests). However, this is a performance/micro-optimization suggestion rather than a clear defect (no correctness, security, or functional bug is demonstrated, and the expected sizes of guests/attendees are typically small). As stated, it’s not a verifiable “problem” beyond potential efficiency improvement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:47,60 — Magic sentinel `0` for "no team"/"no user" (teamId ?? 0, userId || 0) fires real DB lookups against id 0; a booking with null userId surfaces a raw Prisma error from findFirstOrThrow rather than a typed TRPCError.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, both `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` and `booking.userId || 0` are used as fallbacks. This is verifiable in the diff:
- `isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)` / `isTeamOwner(...)` will execute with `teamId=0` when the booking has no team, causing unnecessary/incorrect DB lookups against an impossible/invalid id.
- More importantly, `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` will call `findFirstOrThrow` with `id=0` when `booking.userId` is null/undefined. That will throw a Prisma “record not found” error (not a `TRPCError`), which will bubble up as an untyped/internal error rather than a controlled TRPC error. The code itself indicates this case is possible by using `|| 0` rather than requiring `booking.userId` to be present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:35-40,58-68 — booking.user is fetched with destinationCalendar and credentials (encrypted key blobs) and never read, then a second findFirstOrThrow re-fetches the same organizer. Redundant round-trip plus over-fetch of secrets.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the initial prisma.booking.findFirst includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true }}`. The `booking.user` relation is later read for `booking?.user?.destinationCalendar`, so it’s not “never read”, but `booking.user.credentials` is indeed never used anywhere in the handler. Separately, the code then does a second `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow` to fetch organizer name/email/timeZone/locale, which are already available via the included `booking.user` (Prisma `include` returns user scalar fields by default). That makes the organizer re-fetch a redundant DB round-trip, and the credentials include an unnecessary over-fetch of sensitive blobs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:83-106,145 — Seated events: bare Attendee rows created with no BookingSeat rows and no seatsPerTimeSlot check, though the handler reads the seats fields to decorate the email. Capacity can be exceeded; seat-linked flows see orphan attendees.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation unconditionally appends new `attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and then builds a `CalendarEvent` that includes `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` from `booking.eventType`, but there is no check against `seatsPerTimeSlot` (or any other capacity/seat-availability constraint) before adding guests. Given the codebase clearly supports “seated” semantics (those fields exist and seat-related email templates are present in the emails package), this diff introduces a correctness gap: guests can be added beyond capacity, and seat-specific flows that expect seat accounting to match attendee count will become inconsistent because only attendee rows are created here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:92-106 — booking.responses (which carries the guest list as typed data inside JSON) is not updated, so the two representations diverge; flows that rebuild attendees from responses drop the added guests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `addGuestsHandler` that updates `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and then updates external calendars/emails. Nowhere in the shown code is `booking.responses` read, written, or even included in the Prisma query, and the diff does not establish that `booking.responses` is a second “source of truth” for guest emails or that any flow rebuilds attendees from it. Therefore the claim that “two representations diverge” and that “flows drop the added guests” is not verifiable from this diff and depends on assumptions about code/data not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:124-147 — CalendarEvent is hand-assembled instead of using the shared builder used by handleNewBooking/editLocation; result lacks team, eventTypeId, iCalUID/iCalSequence, bookingFields/responses.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the CalendarEvent `evt` is manually constructed and only includes a subset of properties (title/type/description/start/end/organizer/attendees/uid/etc.). It does not include any `team` info (nor eventTypeId/bookingFields/sequence-like metadata). This is verifiable in the diff and has an observable impact: `sendAddGuestsEmails` checks `calendarEvent.team?.members` to email team members, but since `evt` has no `team`, that branch will never run, so team members won’t be notified for team bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/architecture][lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 — EventManager is built from the acting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)), not the organizer's, though the organizer's credentials are already fetched at :36 and discarded. On exactly the attendee and team-admin paths the handler authorizes, no credential matches booking.references, so the calendar/video update silently no-ops and new guests never get a real calendar invite.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler explicitly authorizes non-organizers (team admin/owner and attendees) to add guests, but then constructs `EventManager` using credentials from the *acting user* (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`), not from the booking’s organizer/booking owner. The booking query earlier includes `user: { ... credentials: true }`, yet those organizer credentials are never used. Given the flow calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` to update the calendar event, this creates a clear risk that for attendee/admin paths the calendar update cannot be performed (because the actor may not own/have credentials for the organizer’s calendar event referenced by `booking.references`), so the calendar sync/invite update may not happen even though the DB attendees are updated. The finding’s statement that organizer credentials were fetched via the separate `organizer` query is slightly off (that query selects only name/email/timeZone/locale), but the core mismatch (discarding organizer credentials and using ctx.user’s) is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/intent] addGuests.handler.ts:138 — Recurring bookings: evt.recurringEvent is populated from the event type so emails/ICS describe a series, but only the single bookingId row is updated; no recurringEventId handling.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code updates attendees only on the single Booking row identified by bookingId (prisma.booking.update where id=bookingId). It also sets evt.recurringEvent from booking.eventType.recurringEvent, which will cause downstream email/ICS generation to potentially include recurrence info. However, the finding’s claim that this is a bug because “only the single bookingId row is updated” assumes a data model where recurring bookings are stored as multiple booking rows requiring recurringEventId-based updates. That model/requirement is not shown in the diff; it’s plausible Cal.com represents a recurring series as one booking with an RRULE, in which case updating one booking row is correct and no recurringEventId handling is needed. Therefore the issue is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:165 — No webhook or workflow trigger fired for the booking change, so integrations and workflows never learn about added guests.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler updates attendees in Prisma, updates the calendar via EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, and sends emails. The diff does not show any existing webhook/workflow trigger mechanism that should be invoked here (nor any established pattern being omitted), so the claim that “integrations and workflows never learn about added guests” is not verifiable from this change alone and depends on external system behavior not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:96 — No bookingReference/metadata update for video providers; Zoom/Meet participant lists are not updated.

adjudication.rationale: The new addGuests handler does update the calendar event via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and passes along existing `booking.references` video call data into `evt.videoCallData`. The diff does not define any required “bookingReference/metadata update” step for Zoom/Meet, nor does it show that participant lists are maintained in booking references/metadata. Claiming Zoom/Meet participant lists won’t be updated is therefore speculative and not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:165 — updateCalendarAttendees is outside any try/catch and runs after the DB commit; a provider failure surfaces as a mutation error even though guests were persisted, with no partial-success feedback.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the attendees are persisted via prisma.booking.update(...) before calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking), and that call is not wrapped in any try/catch (only sendAddGuestsEmails is). If updateCalendarAttendees throws (e.g., external calendar/provider failure), the TRPC mutation will error even though the DB write already happened, creating a partial-success/inconsistent outcome with no handling in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:85 — New guests inherit organizer.locale, so guest-facing emails are localized to the organizer's language rather than defaulting to en.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly added guests are created with `locale: organizer.locale` (in `guestsFullDetails`). Later, when building `attendeesList`, the email language is derived from `attendee.locale ?? "en"`, so these new guests will reliably get the organizer’s locale rather than falling back to English. This behavior is directly introduced by the diff and can lead to guest-facing emails being localized to the organizer’s language even though the guests’ preferred locale is unknown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: (repo-wide) — Zero tests: no unit tests for addGuestsHandler (permissions, dedupe, blacklist, empty-result 400) and no e2e coverage, despite new data-testid attributes (add_members, add-emails, add-another-email) apparently added for them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new functionality (UI dialog, TRPC mutation, handler, email templates) and introduces new `data-testid` attributes, but it does not add any test files or test changes. However, the proposed finding is fundamentally a process/coverage complaint (absence of tests) rather than a verifiable defect in correctness/security/behavior introduced by the diff, and there is no evidence in the diff of a project requirement that would make missing tests itself a concrete bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/completeness] BookingListItem.tsx:193 — The action is appended to editBookingActions unconditionally, which is rendered for past bookings (lines 553-554) and unconfirmed ones, so "Add guests" is offered on past/unconfirmed bookings and fires CONFIRMED invites for events that already happened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/scope][lens/architecture][lens/intent] packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 — Component inside packages/ui imports its own barrel (@calcom/ui) while index.tsx:153 re-exports it: a module cycle that survives only because MultiEmailLazy defers via next/dynamic, and which pulls the whole UI barrel into the lazy chunk. Sibling form components import relatively.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the new `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the component imports UI primitives from the package barrel: `import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui";` (line 2). In the same diff, `packages/ui/index.tsx` now re-exports `MultiEmail` via `export { default as MultiEmail } from "./form/MultiEmailLazy";`, and `MultiEmailLazy` dynamically imports `./MultiEmail`. That creates a verifiable circular dependency path: `MultiEmail -> @calcom/ui (index.tsx) -> MultiEmailLazy -> (dynamic) MultiEmail`. This is a real architectural defect (module cycle) introduced by the diff; sibling form components typically avoid this by using relative imports within `packages/ui`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx:3 — Copy-pasted comment "These are like 40kb that not every user needs" from PhoneInputLazy/AddressInputLazy, which wrap heavy third-party libs; MultiEmail is ~90 lines with no third-party dependency, so both the claim and the extra dynamic-import wrapper are unjustified.

However, the finding’s core claim that the wrapper is “unjustified” is subjective/architectural rather than a verifiable defect, and the “~40kb” statement is not something that can be proven wrong from the diff alone (bundle size depends on build output and transitive imports). adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/architecture] AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — A second, differently-shaped schema is declared in the component body under the same name as the server schema (ZAddGuestsInputSchema), recreated every render, splitting validation ownership — and the client-only copy is the one carrying the uniqueness refine.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `packages/trpc/.../addGuests.schema.ts` shaped as `{ bookingId: number, guests: string[] }`. Separately, `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx` declares a *different* `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` inside the component body as `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` (array-only + uniqueness refine). That client schema is recreated on every render and enforces uniqueness only on the client, while the server schema does not. adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/tasks/task-001.md:1 — The harness task prompt file is committed as repo documentation; it is not part of the feature and should not land.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/completeness] addGuests.handler.ts:170 — console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") discards err and uses console.log rather than the project logger; the handler still returns success, so total email failure is invisible to users and operators.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the sendAddGuestsEmails call is wrapped in try/catch, but the catch block only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not log the caught `err` (no stack/message) or propagate/return an error. The handler then continues and returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so a complete email-send failure would not be surfaced to the caller and would be poorly observable in logs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The most serious items are the security cluster: any attendee can push booking details plus the video URL and meeting password to arbitrary addresses, the unbounded/undeduped guest array with no rate limit turns the endpoint into a mail amplifier, and the missing booking-status guard lets that happen on cancelled bookings. The deterministic gate returned PASS_ADVISORY and found none of these — its own manifest flags shard-01 as unreviewed, so that PASS carries no signal here.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new authed TRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests` whose handler explicitly allows any existing attendee to call it (`isAttendee` check) and then adds arbitrary `guests` emails to the booking and sends calendar/email notifications. The handler builds a `CalendarEvent` that includes `videoCallData` (meeting URL/password) from booking references and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, then emails all attendees via `sendAddGuestsEmails`, so an attendee can cause meeting details to be sent to arbitrary addresses. The server-side input schema has no uniqueness or max-length constraint (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())`), and the handler does not dedupe the provided array (it only filters out existing attendees/blacklisted emails), while `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` uses the original unfiltered list—so the endpoint can be abused to add many recipients (mail amplification). There is also no booking status/state guard in the handler (it fetches by id only and proceeds), so it would operate on cancelled bookings if they exist. The specific claim about “no rate limit” is not directly verifiable from this diff alone, but the other security issues are clearly present.
